issues.body: `LIMIT_KEYS` persists `opus5_premium_window`, but `persist_limits` writes it into a `limits:` line that the diff itself says `select-and-claim._parse_account` ignores. `_probe_account` also does not seed the next observation from that catalog value. Consequently, after one tick proves that an account has (for example) a `7d_oi` bucket, a later transport failure produces only `{"opus5_probe": "error"}`; the window key disappears and `_opus5_eligible` returns `True`. Healthy base 5h/7d values then admit work even if the already-known premium bucket is exhausted. The self-test codifies this fail-open path by expecting transport-error admission, so the claimed durable observation is decorative rather than binding.
issues.fix_hint: Make the persisted discovery an input to subsequent probe/admission records. Once an account has ever declared a premium window, a failed or headerless current probe must retain that known window and fail closed because its current utilization is unreadable. Add a cross-tick test: persist a discovered window, simulate the next opus5 probe failing, load the resulting production inputs, and assert `usage_eligible(..., model="opus5")` is false. Preserve permissive behavior only for accounts for which no premium window has ever been observed.
issues.title: Persisted premium-window discovery is ignored after a probe error

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Request changes: the round-1 base-window defect is fixed, but the new durable-observation path is disconnected from admission. A successful tick can persist that opus5 has a premium bucket, yet the allocator explicitly ignores the persisted field; any later opus5 probe error omits the window from the snapshot and `_opus5_eligible` admits on base headroom. Thus the exact known-bucket cliff this change is meant to prevent reopens on a transient probe failure. Because this is a new blocker relative to round 1, progress is regressing under the required scale.
